rules.description: Complete NGDA noun patterns use the cited Cook class models with each lexical stem. Mass/abstract plural reference cells do not establish new count senses.

Bæð keeps æ in singular and has a in plural baðu/baða/baðum; geat keeps ea in singular and has a in plural gatu/gata/gatum; sīðfæt has sīðfatas/sīðfata/sīðfatum. The changes belong to these checked lexemes, not all written vowels.
Seolh loses h and lengthens eo before case endings: sēol-. Bare nominative/accusative singular retain seolh. This completes a newly used subpattern.
Selected seolfor/frōfor/ceaster/winter use seolfr-/frōfr-/ceastr-/wintr- before endings. Īsern retains its medial e because the second syllable ends in rn; sumer retains its medial vowel.

Sumer and winter retain complete ordinary masculine systems; Cook43.5 also records occasional genitive/dative singular and nominative plural -a. The variants are accepted, not separately tested recall.

All ordinary adjective NGDA cells are productive; distinct instrumental masculine/neuter singular cells remain recognition reference. Blæc changes æ to a before vowel endings; consonantal endings retain æ. Stille/smylte retain final e only where no ending replaces it. Stille simplifies ll before consonantal endings: stilne/stilre/stilra, but stille/stilles/stillum.

The selected complete fæger, gesyndig and ðurstig tables retain the medial vowel. Cook57.3 also licenses syncope and occasional endingless feminine singular/neuter plural; the exact source gesyndge remains a separately supported syncopated realization. Fæger has independently attested retained and syncopated forms.

Dēorwierðra and fægerra are weak throughout, including predicates. Remove final e of dēorwierðe before -ra. Fægerra/fægerre are directly documented by BT264a. Genitive plurals dēorwierðra/fægerra apply the already taught consonant reduction; these full paradigms are rule-derived, not verbatim source tables.
